title: the-decompose-judge-accepts-a-commons-output
intention: judge_decompose's writes_to judge accepts an address inside CairnCommons as well as inside the cairn repo, so a piece whose output lands in the commons (a concept-piece's prose, a node class) is a judged, gated write rather than a red.
why: No concept-piece can be charted today: its only output is a .md in CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code, and both decompose mouths red any writes_to outside the cairn repo, so its chart never berths and its BUILDME entry lane a_berthed_chart_chain_claims_the_ticket never opens. Measured 2026-10-04 at df05d93da4c0's chart. The rule's own why (68f1fc073512: 'a write this system does not gate and git cannot see') is false for the commons, which is git-tracked and whose records pass the artifact door, and Akien answered open-90d38cb2bdca 'a agreed': commons files read as code are proved like code.
traces_to: Akien's answer to CairnCommons/questions/open-90d38cb2bdca.json ('a agreed'); Law 6; Law 9; RULE 1 (inside build_inspector)
how: cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py _writes_to_frags: an entry is in bounds when its normalized path lies under _REPO_ROOT or under _REPO_ROOT.parent / 'CairnCommons'. Anything else still reds, with a sentence naming both roots. A new proof beside it.
falsifier: GREEN when (1) _writes_to_frags over a piece whose writes_to is an absolute path under the commons root draws no finding; (2) /etc/passwd draws one 'outside' finding and so does a path under ~/.cairn; (3) the outside finding's sentence names both the cairn repo and CairnCommons. RED if any fails or test_inspector reds. Horizon: this ticket PROVED and df05d93da4c0's chart berthed once sibling ticket the-decompose-door-accepts-a-commons-output lands.
watchme: none, because df05d93da4c0's chart berthing (CairnCommons/tickets/df05d93da4c0-an-unvouched-green-completes-and-notifies.json) is the first use and is measured at its BUILDME
children: none, because the change is one function and one proof inside build_inspector

decisions.text: D1: SETTLED: in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py _writes_to_frags, after `root = str(_REPO_ROOT)` add `commons = str(_REPO_ROOT.parent / "CairnCommons")`; the in-bounds test becomes `any(resolved == r or resolved.startswith(r + os.sep) for r in (root, commons))` with `resolved = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(root, addr))` unchanged (a relative entry still resolves against the repo). The finding text becomes "sub-problem %d writes_to %r — outside the cairn repo and CairnCommons" (still containing 'outside the cairn repo', so test_inspector.py:417 stays true), evidence gains "commons_root": commons, and why_it_matters reads: "a declared output outside the two roots this system owns is a write it does not gate and git cannot see (Law 6, and the class-space rule that runtime state never lands here); CairnCommons is the second root: git-tracked, its records pass the artifact door (Akien, open-90d38cb2bdca)." The docstring's 'INSIDE the cairn repo' sentence names both roots and cites this ticket.

D2: SETTLED: new proof cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_the_decompose_judge_accepts_a_commons_output.py, the same shape as cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_green_over_a_red_under_other_conditions_notifies.py (docstring, _REPO_ROOT = parents[4] (measured: the first ancestor holding .git; [3] is the cairn package dir), sys.path insert, PROVES dict, main() running each tooth and printing GREEN/RED, exit 1 on any fail). Each tooth imports `from cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector import _REPO_ROOT, _writes_to_frags` inside its body. Teeth: '1' test_a_commons_address_draws_no_finding: `_writes_to_frags(0, {"what": "p", "writes_to": [str(_REPO_ROOT.parent / "CairnCommons" / "intentions-not-beside-code" / "I-x.md")]}) == []`. '2' test_an_address_outside_both_roots_still_reds: for each of "/etc/passwd" and str(Path.home() / ".cairn" / "x.json"), the call returns exactly one frag whose judge is 'decompose_composes_holdings' and whose finding contains 'outside'. '3' test_the_red_names_both_roots: the /etc/passwd frag's finding contains 'cairn repo' and 'CairnCommons'. Validation berths at cairn/machines/build_inspector/validations/ through the tester seal.

D3: SETTLED: why widening the root is a fix and not a weakening: the check exists to refuse a declared output this system does not gate and git cannot see (68f1fc073512); CLAUDE.md berths every concept-piece in CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/, so a root of the cairn repo alone contradicts the design it guards and leaves no concept-piece chartable; CairnCommons is git-tracked and every record write in it passes the artifact door, so it meets the rule's own why exactly as the cairn repo does, while /etc/passwd and instance-space ~/.cairn still fail it and still red.
decisions.step: unlisted: why the second root is sound
